01 / The constraint

The constraint

Search private documents without sending them to a hosted service. The interface, command line and programmatic clients need to expose how retrieval chose its results.

02 / The implementation

What I built

FAISS finds documents with similar meaning through vector search. BM25 ranks exact-term matches. Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines their positions in the two lists. SQLite stores metadata, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server gives clients structured access.

03 / A deliberate choice

The tradeoff

The local store has one writer. That keeps updates and retrieval behaviour easier to inspect, at the cost of distributed scale.

04 / Evidence, with its limits

What the work showed

On a fixed synthetic set of 18 queries, hybrid search kept Hit Rate@3 at 1.000 and raised mean reciprocal rank (MRR) from 0.972 to 1.000. Hit Rate@3 asks whether the expected result appears in the first three; MRR rewards finding it nearer the top. This is a regression guard, not a general quality benchmark.

Hit Rate@31.000
MRR0.972 → 1.000
